records.title: Counterparty launches token issuance on Bitcoin
records.summary: Counterparty launched with XCP distributed through proof of burn on Bitcoin.
records.significance: It demonstrated token issuance and later digital collectibles on Bitcoin years before the modern NFT boom.

records.title: XCoin launches, later becoming Darkcoin and Dash
records.summary: Evan Duffield launched the chain that would become Dash, initially named XCoin and soon renamed Darkcoin.
records.significance: The project became an early privacy- and payments-focused altcoin with an influential masternode/governance model.

records.title: Dogecoin community funds the Jamaican bobsled team
records.summary: The Dogecoin community raised more than 26 million DOGE, worth roughly $25,000 at the time, to support the Jamaican bobsled team's Olympic campaign.
records.significance: The fundraiser proved a joke cryptocurrency could mobilize a global internet community for real-world causes.

sources.title: The Guardian — Dogecoin Jamaican bobsled fundraiser

records.title: Ethereum is publicly unveiled
records.summary: Vitalik Buterin published Ethereum: Now Going Public and presented the project at the North American Bitcoin Conference in Miami.
records.significance: Ethereum moved from a circulated proposal into a public project seeking developers, funding and users.

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation — Ethereum: Now Going Public

records.title: Mt. Gox collapses
records.summary: After halting Bitcoin withdrawals earlier in February, Mt. Gox went offline on 25 February and filed for bankruptcy protection in Tokyo on 28 February.
records.significance: The failure of Bitcoin's former dominant exchange became crypto's defining early custody and counterparty disaster.

records.title: Newsweek claims Dorian Nakamoto created Bitcoin
records.summary: Newsweek published a cover story identifying Dorian Prentice Satoshi Nakamoto as Bitcoin's creator. Dorian denied involvement and the claim was not substantiated.
records.significance: The media frenzy became one of the most famous failed attempts to unmask Satoshi.

sources.title: The Guardian — Dorian Nakamoto denies Bitcoin involvement

records.title: Ethereum Yellow Paper formalizes the protocol
records.summary: Ethereum's official timeline dates Gavin Wood's Yellow Paper to 1 April 2014.
records.significance: The Yellow Paper provided a formal technical specification for Ethereum and the Ethereum Virtual Machine.

records.title: Monero launches
records.summary: Monero launched as a fair-launched CryptoNote-derived privacy cryptocurrency.
records.significance: Monero became the most enduring privacy-focused cryptocurrency and a central case in debates over anonymity, fungibility and regulation.

records.title: Kevin McCoy mints Quantum
records.summary: Kevin McCoy's digital artwork Quantum was minted on the Namecoin blockchain.
records.significance: Quantum is one of the strongest early precedents for blockchain-linked digital art and later NFT culture.

records.title: GHash.io reaches the 51% mining-concentration threshold
records.summary: GHash.io briefly reached or exceeded roughly half of Bitcoin's network hash rate, triggering intense concern about mining concentration.
records.significance: It became Bitcoin's clearest early warning that a mining pool could approach majority control without attacking the network.

records.title: US Marshals auction seized Silk Road Bitcoin
records.summary: The US Marshals Service auctioned 29,656 BTC forfeited from Silk Road infrastructure; Tim Draper was later identified as the winner.
records.significance: The auction was a remarkable early moment in which a government treated seized Bitcoin as a marketable asset.

records.title: Ethereum Ether crowdsale begins
records.summary: Ethereum launched a 42-day Ether genesis sale, accepting Bitcoin and initially offering 2,000 ETH per BTC.
records.significance: The sale funded Ethereum development and became a landmark precursor to the ICO era.

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation — Launching the Ether Sale

records.title: Trezor Model One launches
records.summary: Trezor launched the first commercial hardware wallet.
records.significance: Hardware wallets created a consumer category for isolating private keys from general-purpose computers and normalized safer self-custody.

sources.title: Trezor — ten years since first hardware wallet

records.title: Hal Finney dies
records.summary: Hal Finney died after living with ALS.
records.significance: Finney was a foundational cypherpunk, creator of RPOW, early Bitcoin tester and recipient of the first known Bitcoin transaction.

records.title: First Tether/USDT tokens are issued
records.summary: The project that began as Realcoin issued its first USDT tokens on the Bitcoin/Omni layer and subsequently adopted the Tether name.
records.significance: Tether became the dominant crypto-native dollar instrument and one of the most consequential pieces of exchange infrastructure.

sources.title: Tether — Eight Years of Stability and Innovation

records.title: BitMEX begins live Bitcoin trading
records.summary: BitMEX opened live Bitcoin trading after an earlier beta challenge.
records.significance: BitMEX became a major derivatives venue and later helped popularize perpetual swaps and extreme leverage in crypto.

records.title: Microsoft begins accepting Bitcoin for digital purchases
records.summary: Microsoft allowed US users to add Bitcoin-funded credit for purchases in the Windows and Xbox stores.
records.significance: A global technology company accepting Bitcoin represented a major merchant-adoption milestone.
